proposals.title: Branded numeric types and explicit-mode division helper (ADR-003 + ADR-004)
proposals.why_now: Every subsequent FASE-1 deliverable — ledger entries, price queries, RNG coordinates, the tick loop, order execution — requires the primitive type vocabulary defined in ADR-003 and ADR-004. This work is fully independent of the CanonicalEncoder and can proceed in parallel. Delaying it compounds: every module written without branded types must be retrofitted, and ADR-004 enforcement (division without a declared mode is a compile or lint error) becomes harder to impose after arithmetic code exists. ADR-004 has a DEFINIR item — the technical enforcement mechanism — that requires an ADR before implementation.

proposals.title: Positional RNG (ADR-002): hash function ADR and rand() implementation in packages/core
proposals.why_now: The price generator, macro event scheduler, bot policy derivation, and NPC tip truth all depend on rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates). No world output can be tested and INV-02 and INV-03 cannot be verified without it. The hash function inside rand() is a DEFINIR item — it must be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before implementation, and it cannot be the native hash function. The spec recommends SplitMix64 over FNV-1a. This work depends on branded types (Tick coordinates) and can proceed once IDEA-002 is accepted.

proposals.title: StateHash and SaveHash: ADR and implementation in packages/core
proposals.why_now: StateHash is required by INV-01, INV-22, and the FASE-1 CI gate (replay of three reference games comparing StateHash by tick). Once the CanonicalEncoder is accepted (IDEA-001), StateHash is the immediate next deliverable: it specifies exactly which fields enter the hash, which are explicitly excluded (finalTick, narrative text, cached projections), and how the hash primitive is applied to canonical bytes. Delaying the StateHash ADR after encoder acceptance will block the replay CLI and the CI gate. StateHash and SaveHash are distinct types with distinct computation paths; the ADR must record this separation.

warnings: CanonicalEncoder has been rejected nine times across three task IDs. Each review narrows the remaining issues, but the pattern of accumulated rejections suggests the implementation agent should read the complete review-03 findings verbatim and address them as a checklist before submitting, rather than reasoning from memory about what was fixed in prior attempts.

The hash function used inside rand() (ADR-002) and the hash function applied to canonical bytes for StateHash (ADR-009) are two separate DEFINIR items requiring two separate ADRs. They must not share an implementation or be conflated in authorship. Each must be specified bit-by-bit in its own ADR before implementation.
